record.title: Ø15.0000 open-arch cradle, 149.06° — the motor-support end of the jaw pivot

joins.a: a Ø15.0 cylindrical body laid into the cradle. On this robot that body is the 15x10x3 ball bearing's OUTER RING (part:bearing-15x10x3, interface 'od', Ø15.0 measured on Pollen's own mesh), whose bore carries part:microduck-jaw's Ø10.0000 journal.
joins.b: the cradle: an arch of Ø15.0000 bore swept 149.06° about its axis and cut off flat at the chord plane — part:microduck-motor-support interface 'lens_tube', two ring bands 2.0000 mm and 1.0000 mm long with a 1.0000 mm Ø16.8000 relief between them. Ø15.0000 is the VERTEX figure (free-centre circle fit to the 31 unique vertices at each of four x stations, residual max 0.0000007 mm); the Ø14.9938–14.9978 published here on 2026-09-02 was a chord fit reading one half-sagitta small and is superseded.

record.dof_left_why: MEASURED, and this is the whole point of the folder: the cradle is NOT a bore. cecad.meshslice at x -38.5 finds material only from z 9.5000 to 16.1919 — the arch is cut off flat at z 9.5000 and 210.94° of the circle is open air below. An open arch cannot grip, so it leaves the ring free to turn (rotation_about_z, which is what the jaw pivot is FOR) and free to slide along the axis (translation_along_z: no shoulder, groove or end stop was found on either ring band). It also cannot stop the ring being lifted OUT downward; that is not a DOF in the six-axis vocabulary, so it is stated in `joint.open_direction` and in compat.py rather than hidden. The jaw is held up by its XL330 horn at the other end of the part (jaw.stl, Ø6.0 centre + 4 x Ø2.2 on a Ø12 bolt circle at x ~+42) — this end only locates it.
record.detachable_why: By hand, with no tool and no press: the ring lifts straight out of the open side. That is the honest consequence of a 149.06° arch and it is why this folder is NOT connection:press-fit-bearing-15x10x3, whose seats are 360° pockets and bosses that must be pressed.
record.standard_why: No published standard governs an open cradle of arbitrary included angle. ISO 286 grades bores and shafts; it has nothing to say about an arch that is missing 210.94° of its circle, and quoting it here would be borrowing authority the geometry does not have. compat.py therefore grades DIAMETER and ANGULAR CAPTURE from measurements and refuses to grade grip at all.
record.adds_parts_why: A cradle adds no fastener and no part of its own. The ring it holds is added by connection:press-fit-bearing-15x10x3 (which seats that ring's bore on the jaw journal); adding part:bearing-15x10x3 here as well would double-count it in assembly:microduck's BOM. Nothing is named that this shelf could not resolve.
record.why: THE GEOMETRY IS MEASURED ON BOTH SIDES AND IT AGREES — AND ON 2026-09-03 IT WAS MEASURED AGAIN, BETTER. Cradle: a free-centre circle fitted to the mesh VERTICES at each of the four x stations that carry them (-39.5000, -37.5000, -36.5000, -35.5000; 31 unique vertices each, 124 in all) reads Ø15.000000 with a residual max of 0.0000007 mm, centre (y 0.000000, z 7.500000), arc 149.06° by the meshslice section's angular extent and 149.07° between the first and last vertex of the fit (the 0.01° is where the end vertex falls relative to the cut, not a disagreement about the feature), chord plane z 9.5000, crown z 15.0000, outer surface Ø17.400000. The two ring bands are x -39.5000..-37.5000 (2.0000 mm) and -36.5000..-35.5000 (1.0000 mm) with a 1.0000 mm Ø16.800000 relief between — the band ENDS read by ray-cast intervals at radius 8.100 mm, every DIAMETER read off vertices. Ring: Ø15.000000 OD (part:bearing-15x10x3, re-measured the same way at z 0.3000 and 2.7000, 72 vertices each, residual max 0.0000006 mm), 3.0 wide. Journal through the ring: the jaw's Ø10.000000 boss, centre (y 0.000000, z 7.500000), residual max 0.0000006 mm, x -39.7000..-37.0000 (2.7000 mm) behind a Ø12.000000 x 0.3000 flange. CRADLE AND JOURNAL ARE COAXIAL TO BETTER THAN 0.0000010 mm (their fitted axes differ by 0.000000031 mm, below either fit's own residual — bounded by the instrument, not resolved by it). CRADLE AND RING ARE LINE-TO-LINE: diametral gap 0.0000 mm, zero clearance and zero interference, both sides measured the same way. SUPERSEDED, AND WHY, because an earlier reader was right: the Ø14.9938–14.9978 / Ø11.9949 / Ø17.3926 / Ø16.8007 figures published on 2026-09-02 came from cecad.meshslice cross-section fits, whose point sets mix facet CORNERS (on the cylinder) with edge-interpolated points (inside it by up to one sagitta, 0.00773 mm) — half a sagitta, 0.0039 mm, is exactly the shortfall from Ø15.0000. This folder had ALREADY diagnosed that artefact for its Ø16.8 relief on 2026-09-02 and failed to apply it to its own headline number. With it applied, the derived claim of '0.0000–0.0062 mm of nominal interference' and compat.py's printed diametral_gap_mm -0.0062 describe an interference THAT DOES NOT EXIST. The verdict is unchanged — an arch open over 210.94° cannot grip at any interference — but the number was wrong and is corrected. TWO measured facts are still recorded rather than smoothed: (1) Pollen's MJCF places the bearing GEOM 0.2000 mm above both axes and 0.3000 mm outboard of the journal shoulder — a placement artefact of the visual model, not of the parts; (2) the interface this folder is named from is called 'lens_tube' and its own text called it a lens seat, and that reading is FALSE — in this same frame the m12 lens holder sits at y -52.38..-37.58 and the lens at y -63.8..-44.88, on a different axis 37–64 mm away, with no Ø15 feature anywhere on them. What stays CANNOT DETERMINE is stated per-check in compat.py and as a ledger row: nothing measurable closes the open 210.94°, so the retention of the ring in the cradle cannot be graded from the meshes at all.

joint.default_state: one Ø15.0 ring lying in the arch, free to turn and free to slide; the assembly closes nothing under it in any mesh measured here

axes_cannot_determine.tx: locked only in the +z half-space the arch covers. The arch spans 149.06° centred on +z, so it opposes motion upward and sideways-and-upward; it opposes nothing downward. 'locked' here means 'locked against the arch', and the open direction is named in open_direction.
axes_cannot_determine.tz: recorded as free because NO axial stop was measured on either ring band — no groove, no shoulder, no end face. If the jaw's Ø12.0000 x 0.3000 flange is intended as that stop it would act on the ring's bore side, not in this cradle.

joint.one_way: the cradle resists load only in the closed 149.06°; a downward load lifts the ring out

engagement.band_contact_why: with the ring where Pollen's MJCF puts it (x -40.0000..-37.0000) only the first band (-39.5000..-37.5000) touches it: 2.0000 mm of the ring's 3.0000 mm width, 66.7%. The second band (-36.5000..-35.5000) is clear of the ring by 0.5000 mm. Seat the ring instead against the jaw's flange (x -39.7000..-36.7000) and the numbers become 1.8000 mm on band one and 0.2000 mm on band two — which datum is intended is not stated anywhere in the reference.

rating.retention_why: MISSING and unmeasurable from geometry: an open cradle's holding force is whatever closes it, and nothing in any of Pollen's four MJCF files closes this one.
rating.bore_d_mm_basis: free-centre circle fit to the mesh vertices at four x stations, 2026-09-03: identical to 8 dp at every station (Ø15.00000018), residual max 0.0000007 mm. The span is not a range of readings, it is one reading taken four times. Supersedes Ø14.9938–14.9978 (chord fit).
rating.diametral_gap_why: ring Ø15.000000 minus cradle Ø15.000000, both vertex-measured: LINE-TO-LINE. There is no interference here and none is claimed.

joint.why: holds_by form: what holds the ring is the arch's shape, not friction. The cradle and the ring are LINE-TO-LINE — diametral gap 0.0000 mm, both sides vertex-measured — so there is no interference at all over the 149.07° that exists, and none is claimed. (The '0.0000–0.0062 mm of nominal interference' written here on 2026-09-02 was an artefact of chord-fitting the cradle and vertex-measuring the ring; corrected 2026-09-03.) driven false: the jaw is driven by its XL330 at the other end (the horn face measured on jaw.stl at x ~+42: Ø6.0 centre bore + 4 x Ø2.2 on a Ø12.0 bolt circle). This end is the idler.
